plan: 1 Samuel 26:1-25; 1 Samuel 27:1-7; 1 Chronicles 12:1-7; 1 Samuel 27:8-12; 1 Samuel 28:1-25; 1 Samuel 29:1-11; 1 Chronicles 12:19; Psalm 56:1-13

readings.title: The Ziphite Instigation
readings.subtitle: Sha’ul resumes his systemic pursuit of the anointed king.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 26:1] And the Ziphites came to Sha’ul at Giḇ‘ah, saying, “Is not Daviḏ hiding himself in the hill of Ḥaḵilah, overlooking the wasteland?” [2] And Sha’ul rose up and went down to the Wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men of Yisra’ĕl, to seek Daviḏ in the Wilderness of Ziph. [3] And Sha’ul encamped in the hill of Ḥaḵilah, overlooking the wasteland, by the way, while Daviḏ was dwelling in the wilderness, and he saw that Sha’ul came after him into the wilderness. [4] And Daviḏ sent out spies, and learned that Sha’ul had indeed come. [5] And Daviḏ rose up and came to the place where Sha’ul had encamped. And Daviḏ saw the place where Sha’ul lay, and Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, the commander of his army. And Sha’ul was lying within the enclosure, with the people encamped all around him.

readings.title: Penetrating the Adversary's Camp
readings.subtitle: Daviḏ actively refuses retributive action, leaving the execution of justice to YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 26:6] And Daviḏ spoke up and said to Aḥimeleḵ the Ḥittite and to Aḇishai son of Tseruyah, brother of Yo’aḇ, saying, “Who does go down with me to Sha’ul in the camp?” And Aḇishai said, “I, I go down with you.” [7] And Daviḏ and Aḇishai came to the people by night and saw Sha’ul lying asleep within the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head, and Aḇnĕr and the people lay all around him. [8] And Aḇishai said to Daviḏ, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has surrendered your enemy into your hand this day. And now, please, let me strike him at once with the spear, right into the earth, and not a second time!” [9] But Daviḏ said to Aḇishai, “Do not destroy him, for who shall stretch out his hand against <dn>את</dn> the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and be guiltless?” [10] Daviḏ also said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, except <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does smite him, or his day come that he shall die, or he shall go out to battle and perish, [11] far be it from me, by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that I stretch out my hand against <dn>את</dn> the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And now, please take <dn>את</dn> the spear and <dn>את</dn> the jug of water that are by his head, and let us go.” [12] So Daviḏ took <dn>את</dn> the spear and <dn>את</dn> the jug of water by Sha’ul’s head, and they went away. And no man saw it or knew it or awoke, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had fallen on them.

readings.title: Exposing the Fleshly Guard
readings.subtitle: Daviḏ highlights the failure of human strength to protect the sovereign.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 26:13] And Daviḏ passed over to the other side, and stood on the top of a hill far away, a great distance being between them. [14] And Daviḏ called out to the people and to Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, saying, “Do you not answer, Aḇnĕr?” And Aḇnĕr answered and said, “Who are you, calling out to the sovereign?” [15] And Daviḏ said to Aḇnĕr, “Are you not a man? And who is like you in Yisra’ĕl? Why then have you not guarded <dn>את</dn> your master the sovereign? For one of the people came in to destroy your master the sovereign. [16] “What you have done is not good. As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, you are worthy to die, because you have not guarded <dn>את</dn> your master, <dn>את</dn> the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And now see where the sovereign’s spear is, and the jug of water that was by his head.”

readings.subsection: The Appeal to the Righteous Judge
readings.title: The Plea for Premial Justice
readings.subtitle: Daviḏ proclaims his innocence and seeks restorative intervention over retributive exile.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 26:17] And Sha’ul recognised Daviḏ’s voice, and said, “Is that your voice, my son Daviḏ?” And Daviḏ said, “It is my voice, my master, O sovereign.” [18] And he said, “Why is this that my master is pursuing his servant? For what have I done, or what evil is in my hand? [19] “And now, please, let my master the sovereign hear the words of his servant: If <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has moved you against me, let <dn>Him</dn> accept an offering. But if it is the children of men, then they are cursed before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for they have driven me out today that I should not join myself to the inheritance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, ‘Go, serve other mighty ones.’ [20] “And now, do not let my blood fall to the earth before the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. For the sovereign of Yisra’ĕl has come out to seek a flea, as when one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”

readings.subsection: The Appeal to the Righteous Judge
readings.title: A Fleeting Confession
readings.subtitle: Sha’ul admits his error, while Daviḏ trusts solely in the guarantee of the Elohim.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 26:21] And Sha’ul said, “I have sinned. Come back, my son Daviḏ. For no more am I going to do evil to you, because my life was precious in your eyes today. See, I have acted foolishly, and have greatly strayed.” [22] And Daviḏ answered and said, “See, the sovereign’s spear! And let one of the young men come over and get it. [23] “And let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> reward every man for his righteousness and his trustworthiness, for this day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave you into my hand, but I would not stretch out my hand against <dn>את</dn> the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [24] “And see, as your life has been valued in my eyes today, so let my life be valued in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and let <dn>Him</dn> deliver me out of all distress.” [25] And Sha’ul said to Daviḏ, “Blessed are you, my son Daviḏ, achieving much, and indeed prevailing!” Then Daviḏ went on his way, and Sha’ul returned to his place.

readings.title: Seeking Asylum in Gath
readings.subtitle: Driven by the reality of systemic disharmony, Daviḏ maneuvers strategically into Philistine territory.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 27:1] And Daviḏ said in his heart, “Now I shall perish by the hand of Sha’ul, some day. There is naught better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Sha’ul shall give up searching for me any longer in any part of Yisra’ĕl, and I shall escape out of his hand.” [2] So Daviḏ rose up and passed over with the six hundred men who were with him to Aḵish son of Ma‛oḵ, sovereign of Gath. [3] And Daviḏ dwelt with Aḵish at Gath, he and his men, each man with his household – Daviḏ with his two wives, Aḥino‛am the Yizre‛ĕlitess, and Aḇiḡayil the Karmelitess, Naḇal’s widow. [4] And it was reported to Sha’ul that Daviḏ had fled to Gath, so he sought him no more. [5] And Daviḏ said to Aḵish, “If I have now found favour in your eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, to dwell there. For why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?” [6] And Aḵish gave him Tsiqlaḡ that day. That is why Tsiqlaḡ has belonged to the sovereigns of Yehuḏah to this day. [7] And the time that Daviḏ dwelt in the country of the Philistines came to be a year and four new moons.

readings.title: The Benjamite Defectors
readings.subtitle: Elite warriors from Sha’ul’s own tribe recognize the shift in authority and align with Daviḏ.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 12:1] Now these are they who came to Daviḏ at Tsiqlaḡ while he was still in hiding from Sha’ul son of Qish. And they were among the mighty men, helping the battle, [2] armed with bows, using both the right hand and the left, with stones, and with arrows, with bows, of the brothers of Sha’ul, of Binyamin. [3] The chief was Aḥi‛ezer and Yo’ash, the sons of Shema‛ah the Giḇ‛athite; and Yezav’ĕl and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth; and Beraḵah, and Yĕhu the Anathothite; [4] and Yishmayah the Giḇ‛onite, a mighty man among the thirty, and over the thirty; and Yirmeyah, and Yaḥazi’ĕl, and Yoḥanan, and Yozaḇaḏ the Geḏĕrathite; [5] Eluzai, and Yerimoth, and Be‛alyah, and Shemaryahu, and Shephatyahu the Ḥaruphite; [6] Elqanah, and Yishshiyahu, and Azar’ĕl, and Yov‛ezer, and Yashoḇ‛am the Qorḥites; [7] and Yo’ĕlah and Zeḇaḏyah, the sons of Yeroḥam of Geḏor.

readings.title: The Strategic Diversion
readings.subtitle: Daviḏ secures his position by operating a localized campaign against ancient adversaries.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 27:8] And Daviḏ and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, and the Girzites, and the Amalĕqites. For those nations were the inhabitants of the land from of old, as you go to Shur, even as far as the land of Mitsrayim. [9] And when Daviḏ had stricken the land, he left neither man nor woman alive, but took away sheep, and cattle, and donkeys, and camels, and garments, and returned and came to Aḵish. [10] And Aḵish would say, “Where have you made a raid today?” And Daviḏ would say, “Against the South of Yehuḏah, or against the South of the Yeraḥme’ĕlites, or against the South of the Qĕynites.” [11] Daviḏ did not keep alive man nor woman, to bring news to Gath, saying, “Lest they inform against us, saying, ‘Thus Daviḏ did.’ ” And this was his practice all the days that he dwelt in the country of the Philistines. [12] And Aḵish trusted Daviḏ, saying to himself, “He has indeed made himself a stench to his people in Yisra’ĕl, and has become my servant forever.”

readings.title: The Philistine Mobilization
readings.subtitle: Facing the adversary's armies, Sha’ul finds YeHoVaH's face completely hidden.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 28:1] And it came to be in those days that the Philistines gathered their armies for battle, to fight with Yisra’ĕl. And Aḵish said to Daviḏ, “You know, of course, that you are to go out with me in the army, you and your men.” [2] And Daviḏ said to Aḵish, “Very well, you shall know what your servant should do.” And Aḵish said to Daviḏ, “Very well, I make you one of my chief guardians forever.” [3] And Shemu’ĕl had died, and all Yisra’ĕl had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, in his own city. And Sha’ul had put away <dn>את</dn> the mediums and <dn>את</dn> the spiritists from the land. [4] And the Philistines were gathered, and came and encamped at Shunĕm. And Sha’ul gathered all Yisra’ĕl, and they encamped at Gilboa. [5] And when Sha’ul saw the army of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly. [6] And Sha’ul inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did not answer him, either by dreams or by Urim or by the prophets.

readings.title: Seeking the Medium of Ĕn Dor
readings.subtitle: In systemic collapse, the king abandons Torah to consult the unauthorized spiritual realm.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 28:7] Sha’ul then said to his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, to go to her and inquire of her.” And his servants said to him, “Look, there is a woman who is a medium at Ĕn Dor.” [8] And Sha’ul disguised himself and put on other garments, and went, he and two men with him. And they came to the woman by night. And he said, “Please divine for me, and bring up for me the one I shall name.” [9] But the woman said to him, “Look, you know what Sha’ul has done, how he has cut off <dn>את</dn> the mediums and <dn>את</dn> the spiritists from the land. Why then do you lay a snare for my life, to put me to death?” [10] And Sha’ul swore to her by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, no punishment comes upon you for this matter.” [11] And the woman said, “Whom do I bring up for you?” So he said, “Bring up <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl for me.” [12] And when the woman saw <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl, she cried out with a loud voice. And the woman spoke to Sha’ul, saying, “Why have you deceived me? You yourself are Sha’ul!” [13] And the sovereign said to her, “Do not be afraid. What did you see?” And the woman said to Sha’ul, “I saw a spirit coming up out of the earth.” [14] And he said to her, “What is his form?” And she said, “An old man is coming up, and he is covered with a mantle.” And Sha’ul knew that it was Shemu’ĕl, and he bowed with his face to the ground and did obeisance.

readings.title: The Transfer of Authority
readings.subtitle: Shemu’ĕl confirms the kingdom has been legally torn away due to rebellion against YeHoVaH's commands.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 28:15] And Shemu’ĕl said to Sha’ul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” And Sha’ul answered, “I am deeply distressed, for the Philistines are fighting against me, and <dn>Elohim</dn> has turned aside from me and does not answer me any more, neither by prophets nor by dreams. So I have called you, to reveal to me what I should do.” [16] Then Shemu’ĕl said, “And why do you ask me, seeing <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has turned aside from you and has become your enemy? [17] <dq>“And </dq><dn><dq>YeHoVaH</dq></dn><dq> has done for </dq><dn><dq>Himself</dq></dn><dq> as </dq><dn><dq>He</dq></dn><dq> spoke by me. For </dq><dn><dq>YeHoVaH</dq></dn><dq> has torn </dq><dn><dq>את</dq></dn><dq> the reign out of your hand and given it to your neighbour, to Daviḏ. </dq>[18] <dq>“Because you did not obey the voice of </dq><dn><dq>YeHoVaH</dq></dn><dq> nor execute </dq><dn><dq>את</dq></dn><dq> </dq><dn><dq>His</dq></dn><dq> burning wrath upon Amalĕq, therefore </dq><dn><dq>YeHoVaH</dq></dn><dq> has done this matter to you today. </dq>[19] <dq>“Further, </dq><dn><dq>YeHoVaH</dq></dn><dq> also gives </dq><dn><dq>את</dq></dn><dq> Yisra’ĕl with </dq><dn><dq>את</dq></dn><dq> you into the hand of the Philistines. And tomorrow you and your sons are with me. </dq><dn><dq>YeHoVaH</dq></dn><dq> also gives </dq><dn><dq>את</dq></dn><dq> the army of Yisra’ĕl into the hand of the Philistines.”</dq>

readings.title: The Collapse of a King
readings.subtitle: Devoid of divine sustenance and paralyzed by fear, Sha’ul faces his impending doom.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 28:20] And immediately Sha’ul fell on the ground, his complete length, and greatly feared because of the words of Shemu’ĕl. And there was no strength in him, for he had eaten no food all day or all night. [21] And the woman came to Sha’ul and saw that he had been greatly disturbed, and said to him, “See, your female servant has obeyed your voice, and I have put my life in my hands and have listened to the words which you spoke to me. [22] “And now, please listen to the voice of your female servant too, and let me set a piece of bread before you. And eat, so that you have strength when you go on your way.” [23] But he refused and said, “I am not going to eat.” But his servants, together with the woman, urged him. And he listened to their voice. So he rose from the ground and sat on the bed. [24] And the woman had a fatted calf in the house, and she quickly slaughtered it. And she took flour and kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread from it. [25] And she brought it before Sha’ul and his servants. And they ate, and rose up and went away that night.

readings.title: The Adversary's Suspicion
readings.subtitle: The Philistine commanders refuse to march with Yisra’ĕl’s true anointed.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 29:1] And the Philistines gathered all their armies at Aphĕq, while Yisra’ĕl encamped by a fountain which is in Yizre‛ĕl. [2] And the princes of the Philistines were passing on by hundreds and by thousands, and Daviḏ and his men were passing on in the rear with Aḵish. [3] And the princes of the Philistines said, “Who are these Hebrews?” And Aḵish said to the princes of the Philistines, “Is this not Daviḏ, the servant of Sha’ul sovereign of Yisra’ĕl, who has been with me these days, or these years? And to this day I have found no evil in him since he came over.” [4] But the princes of the Philistines were wroth with him, and the princes of the Philistines said to him, “Send the man back, let him return to the place which you have appointed for him, and do not let him go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he become our adversary. For with what could he appease his master, if not with the heads of these men? [5] “Is this not Daviḏ, of whom they sang to each other in dances, saying, ‘Sha’ul struck his thousands, and Daviḏ his ten thousands’?”

readings.title: Dismissed from the Ranks
readings.subtitle: Aḵish dismisses Daviḏ, unwittingly preserving the structural integrity of his future reign.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 29:6] And Aḵish called Daviḏ and said to him, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, you have been straight, and your going out and your coming in with me in the army is good in my eyes. For to this day I have not found evil in you since the day of your coming to me. But in the eyes of the princes you are not good. [7] “And now, return, and go in peace, and do no evil in the eyes of the princes of the Philistines.” [8] And Daviḏ said to Aḵish, “But what have I done? And to this day what have you found in your servant as long as I have been with you, that I should not go and fight against the enemies of my master the sovereign?” [9] But Aḵish answered and said to Daviḏ, “I know that you are as good in my eyes as a messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn>, but the princes of the Philistines have said, ‘Let him not go up with us to the battle.’ [10] “And now, rise early in the morning with your master’s servants who have come with you. And as soon as you are up early in the morning and have light, then go.” [11] And Daviḏ and his men rose up early to go in the morning, to return to the land of the Philistines, and the Philistines went up to Yizre‛ĕl.

readings.title: The Menashsheh Defection
readings.subtitle: Additional warriors abandon the failing administration to join the true anointed.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 12:19] And some from Menashsheh went over to Daviḏ when he was going with the Philistines to battle against Sha’ul. But they did not help them, for the princes of the Philistines took advice and sent him away, saying, “He might go over to his master Sha’ul with our heads!”

readings.title: Surrounded by the Flesh
readings.subtitle: Daviḏ leans his full weight upon Elohim’s structural promises amidst systemic oppression.
readings.text: [Psalm 56:1] Show me favour, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, For man would swallow me up; Fighting all day long, he oppresses me. [2] My enemies would swallow me up all day long, For many are fighting against me, O Most High. [3] In the day I am afraid, I trust in <dn>You</dn>. [4] In <dn>Elohim</dn>, whose Word I praise, In <dn>Elohim</dn> I have trusted; I do not fear; What could flesh do to me?

readings.title: The Accounting of Tears
readings.subtitle: Absolute confidence that YeHoVaH meticulously tracks every instance of injustice.
readings.text: [Psalm 56:5] All day long they twist my words; All their thoughts are against me for evil. [6] They stir up strife, they hide, They watch my steps, As they lie in wait for my life. [7] Because of wickedness, cast them out. Put down the peoples in displeasure, O <dn>Elohim</dn>! [8] <dn>You</dn> have counted my wanderings; <dn>You</dn> put <dn>את</dn> my tears into <dn>Your</dn> bottle; Are they not in <dn>Your</dn> book? [9] My enemies turn back in the day I call; This I know, because <dn>Elohim</dn> is for me.

readings.title: Walking in the Light
readings.subtitle: A vow of praise to YeHoVaH for preserving life and maintaining functional harmony.
readings.text: [Psalm 56:10] In <dn>Elohim</dn>, whose Word I praise, In <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, whose Word I praise, [11] In <dn>Elohim</dn> I have trusted; I do not fear; What could man do to me? [12] On me, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, are <dn>Your</dn> vows; I render praises to <dn>You</dn>, [13] For <dn>You</dn> have delivered <dn>את</dn> my life from death, <dn>את</dn> My feet from stumbling, That I might walk before <dn>Elohim</dn>, In the light of the living!
